- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% of spike magnitude.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion in 10–15 day horizons; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to 10-day forecasts if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight by 20–30%.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), model often fails to capture breakout; add 1–2% upward bias to 15–30 day forecasts.
- If sentiment is weak or flat (≤0.33 for 3+ days), model tends to overcorrect downward; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
